message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how you can launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU (or the closest supported GPU if the exact model isn’t available) and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.

> ⚠️ **Important note** – Google Cloud does **not** offer the NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU directly.  
> The closest equivalent that is currently available is the **NVIDIA Tesla A100** (or the older **Tesla V100** if you need a lower‑tier option).  
> If you absolutely need an RTX A6000, you would have to bring your own hardware or use a different provider that supports that GPU.

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2️⃣  Create a new instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-instance \
  --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --boot-disk-device-name=rtx-a6000-disk \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --labels=purpose=ai-workload,gpu=tesla-a100 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: custom init script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds a GPU. Replace `nvidia-tesla-a100` with `nvidia-tesla-v100` if you prefer the older GPU. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a shell script at first boot (e.g., install CUDA, drivers). |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs, just increase the `count=` value.  
> **Tip:** Use `--preemptible` if you want a cheaper, short‑lived instance.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the API directly (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), here’s the exact JSON payload you’d POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
```

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-instance",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "labels": {
    "purpose": "ai-workload",
    "gpu": "tesla-a100"
  },
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> **Replace** `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual values.  
> **Authentication** – You’ll need a valid OAuth 2.0 token with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.

---

## 3. Quick “one‑liner” using `curl`

```bash
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances"
```

Where `instance.json` contains the JSON payload shown above.

---

## 4. Post‑Launch Steps

1. **Install NVIDIA drivers** (if not already installed by the image):
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get update
   sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470
   ```
2. **Verify GPU visibility**:
   ```bash
   nvidia-smi
   ```
3. **Install CUDA Toolkit** (if you plan to run GPU workloads):
   ```bash
   sudo apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-4
   ```

---

## 5. Cost Considerations

| Item | Approximate hourly cost (USD) |
|------|------------------------------|
| `n1-standard-8` VM | $0.40–$0.50 |
| `nvidia-tesla-a100` GPU | $2.50–$3.00 |
| SSD boot disk (200 GB) | $0.10–$0.15 |
| **Total** | ~$3.00–$3.65 per hour |

> **Tip:** Enable **preemptible** VMs if you can tolerate interruptions; they’re ~70% cheaper.

---

## 6. Summary

- **Command‑line**: `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1`
- **REST API**: POST to `/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances` with JSON payload.
- **GPU**: Use `nvidia-tesla-a100` (closest to RTX A6000) or `nvidia-tesla-v100`.
- **OS**: Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (`ubuntu-2004-lts` image family).

Feel free to copy the snippets into your scripts or terminal, adjust the parameters to fit your workload, and hit **Enter**! 🚀
